relation_statement: A document's attention output must be invariant to packing, i.e. rotary positions restart at each document boundary, under guard: cu_doc_lens provided.
observable_signal: Rotary phase / attention output of a document when packed vs standalone.
validity_precondition: multiple documents packed with cu_doc_lens, non-fused RotaryEmbedding path
evidence_from_issue: Per-document RoPE positions not propagated when cu_doc_lens is provided in packed mode
evidence_from_fix: Attention.forward called self.rope without forwarding cu_doc_lens, so later docs got global positions

relation_statement: The scheduler's peak learning rate must equal the user-configured optimizer learning rate rather than a hard-coded default.
observable_signal: applied param-group lr trajectory vs the lr the user configured on the optimizer (observed pinned to 0.001)
validity_precondition: WarmupLR used without an explicit warmup_max_lr in the scheduler config
evidence_from_issue: WarmupLR ignores optimizer LR, always uses hardcoded 0.001
evidence_from_fix: warmup_max_lr defaults to 0.001 instead of inheriting from optimizer param_groups

relation_statement: The attention gate tensor must be sliced to align with each TP rank's query/key/value partition when output_gate is enabled and num_query_groups < tp_size.
observable_signal: slice range/extent of the gate tensor applied on each TP rank versus that rank's query-group partition extent
validity_precondition: self-attention modules with output_gate=True and num_query_groups < tensor_model_parallel_size
evidence_from_issue: MoE/DSA gate not sliced when num_query_groups < tp_size
evidence_from_fix: the gate tensor was not sliced per TP rank; each TP rank multiplied its query/key/value partition by the full unsliced gate, producing wrong attention output but no error

relation_statement: Padded positions must be excluded from label offsetting and remain at the ignore index under guard that fused-boundary label offsets are applied to variable-length batches.
observable_signal: label entries at byte_mask-invalid (padded) positions differing from the ignore_index
validity_precondition: fused-boundary label construction on batches containing padded byte positions
evidence_from_issue: shift_boundary_mask did not AND with byte_mask — pad positions polluted label offsets
evidence_from_fix: padded positions with leftover True boundary_mask received the vocab offset on labels that should have remained at ignore_index, distorting CE on padded positions

relation_statement: The quantized all-to-all reduction result must match the standard gradient reduction (within quantization error) for any actual GPUs-per-node count, i.e., buffer slicing must use the real local world size.
observable_signal: kernel divisor (gpu_per_node) vs actual local_world_size; reduced gradient mismatch against unquantized allreduce on non-16-GPU nodes
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with quantized gradients (qgZ) on nodes whose local world size != 16
evidence_from_issue: all_to_all_quant_reduce hard-codes gpu_per_node=16 — wrong intra-node split on every non-16-GPU node
evidence_from_fix: C++ side ignored the passed local_world_size; buffer slicing done with the wrong divisor attributes rows to the wrong intra-node rank, producing wrong reduced gradients

relation_statement: The number of experts selected per token by group-limited routing must equal the configured top-k under grouped MoE routing.
observable_signal: Per-token count of selected experts (and per-group selection counts) compared to the configured topk; selecting num_groups instead of topk witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: MoE router using group_limited_topk (grouped/device-limited routing)
evidence_from_issue: group_limited_topk uses num_groups instead of topk in inner topk
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: wrong k passed to the inner topk call)

relation_statement: The runtime sequence-parallel communication dtype must equal the user-configured seq_parallel_communication_data_type whenever that key is set.
observable_signal: dtype of sequence-parallel communication buffers compared against the configured value
validity_precondition: user sets seq_parallel_communication_data_type in the config
evidence_from_issue: seq_parallel_communication_data_type config key typo causes silent ignore
evidence_from_fix: constant uses 'seq_parallel_comm_data_type' but config uses 'seq_parallel_communication_data_type'

relation_statement: The per-rank loss must be scaled by the expert-parallel group size before backward so that reduced expert gradients match the ep_size=1 equivalent.
observable_signal: reduced expert-gradient norm smaller by factor ep_size relative to the dense/ep=1 baseline; loss scale factor applied in backward vs ep_size
validity_precondition: AutoEP MoE layer under ZeRO stage 2 where each EP rank sees a token slice of one logical batch
evidence_from_issue: forgets to scale per-rank loss by EP-group size — expert gradients undercount by factor ep_size
evidence_from_fix: backward() does not multiply the loss by ep_size, so reduced expert gradients are scaled by 1/ep_size relative to the ep_size=1 baseline, biasing every step

relation_statement: Under Post-LN (norm_after), the attention normalization must be applied to the attention output immediately before the residual add — not to the QKV projection output — in every transformer block.
observable_signal: Statistics (variance/RMS) of the tensor added to the residual stream: an unnormalized attention output entering the residual add under norm_after witnesses the misplaced norm.
validity_precondition: model.norm_after=true in the sequential transformer block forward
evidence_from_issue: norm_after path applies attn_norm to (att_proj output) instead of to the attention output, leaving residual unnormed
evidence_from_fix: attn_norm was applied to the QKV projection output before attention; Post-LN requires applying attn_norm to the attention output before the residual add — silently changes model semantics

relation_statement: The global gradient norm must aggregate the contributions of all tensor-parallel shards (counting replicated params once and sliced params from every rank) before clipping is applied.
observable_signal: reported total grad norm vs norm recomputed from gathered full gradients; systematic ratio ~1/sqrt(tp_size)
validity_precondition: fp16 fused optimizer with param groups containing genuinely TP-sliced parameters
evidence_from_issue: grad-norm reduces only TP-rank-0 gradients — TP grad_norm undercounted by sqrt(tp_size)
evidence_from_fix: treated the whole flat buffer as non-TP so only tp_rank=0 contributed; for TP-sliced parameters all per-rank slices should sum into the global norm, so clipping is weaker than configured

relation_statement: The dtype used to cast the input activation must equal the actual (post-wrapping) parameter dtype under guard that the module is wrapped by a sharding framework after construction.
observable_signal: dtype of the tensor entering the kernel compared against the live conv weight dtype at forward time
validity_precondition: sequence-mixer modules whose parameters are re-wrapped (FSDP/FSDP2) after construction, mixed-precision params
evidence_from_issue: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
evidence_from_fix: self.dtype was a construction-time snapshot; after FSDP wrapping the actual parameter dtype changed, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision

relation_statement: The scheduler's LR list must contain exactly one scalar entry per optimizer parameter group at every scheduler query under multi-group optimizers.
observable_signal: length and element type of get_lr() output compared against the number of optimizer param groups
validity_precondition: WarmupCosineLR with an optimizer having more than one parameter group
evidence_from_issue: WarmupCosineLR multi-group initialization returns wrong-length LR list
evidence_from_fix: get_lr_ratio returns [0.0] list instead of 0.0 scalar; get_lr returns [0.0] instead of per-group list

relation_statement: The readout (MuReadout) weights must retain the muP prescribed zero/special init and not be overwritten by generic truncated-normal init under guard: use_mup enabled.
observable_signal: ff_proj weight values/std after reset_parameters vs muP prescribed zero init.
validity_precondition: OLMoSequentialBlock with use_mup=True (or full_megatron init) where ff_proj is a MuReadout
evidence_from_issue: Block readout init unconditionally re-initializes ff_proj, overwriting muP zero-init
evidence_from_fix: unconditional init_normal overwrote MuReadout zero init, breaking muP coordinate-check guarantee

relation_statement: The readout ff_out must be created on the configured init_device and receive the designed init scale, not default kaiming init, under guard: meta-init with FSDP.
observable_signal: ff_out weight std and device vs the model's init pipeline output.
validity_precondition: init_device='meta', FSDP enabled (lazy materialization expected)
evidence_from_issue: ff_out nn.Linear constructed without device=init_device, breaking meta-init flow
evidence_from_fix: omitted device kwarg for ff_out so it got default kaiming init on default device, escaping init pipeline

relation_statement: Expert supervision label indices must fall within the range of active experts of the deployed model under guard that routing labels are generated by the data collator.
observable_signal: max expert-label index vs number of active experts; an expert-label slot that never receives router probability mass or gradient
validity_precondition: SFT with expert-routing supervision; data sources mapped by the collator's source-to-expert table
evidence_from_issue: DataCollator routed academic/technical sources to a non-existent 4th expert label
evidence_from_fix: the one-hot at index 3 pointed to an unused expert slot while only 3 experts were active, so router supervision was silently directed to a slot the router never produced gradient for

relation_statement: Reduced gradients on the destination rank must be numerically equivalent whether the configured single-rank reduce path or the bucket allreduce path is used.
observable_signal: gradient checksum difference between runs with use_multi_rank_bucket_allreduce=False vs True
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with use_multi_rank_bucket_allreduce=False
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO2 allreduce_bucket forces rank=None, never uses single-rank reduce path
evidence_from_fix: a hard `rank = None` reset at the top of the function silently overrides any rank passed in; the intended single-destination reduce path is never taken, producing different numerics on the receiving rank

relation_statement: Each tensor-parallel rank's non-expert parameter shard must be saved and restored to the same rank after a checkpoint round trip when expert parallelism is enabled.
observable_signal: count of per-mp-rank model_states files vs tp_size at save; per-TP-rank parameter checksum before save vs after load
validity_precondition: MoE model with expert parallelism and tensor parallel size > 1 during checkpoint save/load
evidence_from_issue: MOE save_checkpoint with TP > 1 only writes mp_rank_00_model_states.pt — non-zero TP ranks lose non-MoE weights
evidence_from_fix: short-circuited with `if exp_dp_rank != 0: return` before saving per-mp-rank files; resuming silently loaded mp_rank_00 onto every TP rank

relation_statement: The loss normalization divisor must be strictly positive so the normalized loss stays finite under guard that instance masking may remove all tokens on a rank.
observable_signal: batch token-count-for-loss equal to 0 on a rank, or NaN in the reported loss
validity_precondition: instance masking enabled; batches where all instances on a rank can be masked
evidence_from_issue: NaN loss when all instances on a rank are masked — division by zero
evidence_from_fix: batch_num_tokens_for_loss = 0 when all instances masked, causing loss / 0 = NaN

relation_statement: The write of the next gradient bucket into the shared reduction buffer must be ordered after the in-flight allreduce finishes reading that buffer, under overlapped communication.
observable_signal: loss/gradient divergence between overlap_comm=True and overlap_comm=False runs on identical inputs; buffer overwritten while a reduction on it is still pending
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with overlap_comm=True and per-bucket allreduce slower than the next bucket's backward compute
evidence_from_issue: reduction stream not waited by current stream — ipg_buffer rewrite races allreduce when comm > compute
evidence_from_fix: current_stream did NOT wait_stream(reduction_stream); the next gradient gets written into the same buffer slot the allreduce is still reading, corrupting the reduce input

relation_statement: The model's eos_token_id must equal the tokenizer's actual EOS id under guard: dolma/GPT-NeoX tokenizer.
observable_signal: Document-boundary/loss-mask token id used vs tokenizer eos_token_id (50279).
validity_precondition: scripts/ladder.py builds 150M config with dolma/GPT-NeoX tokenizer
evidence_from_issue: Ladder script uses eos_token_id=0 instead of dolma tokenizer's 50279
evidence_from_fix: hard-coded eos_token_id=0 treats an ordinary BPE token as boundary and never recognizes real EOS

relation_statement: An encoder rank receiving gradients from multiple decoder TP ranks must average (not sum) them so the boundary gradient is not scaled by the TP fanout factor.
observable_signal: encoder-side received gradient norm vs mean of decoder-side sent gradients (inflated by the TP-fanout factor)
topology_scope: PP>1 with encoder TP < decoder TP
validity_precondition: encoder-decoder pipeline boundary where one encoder TP rank receives gradients from multiple decoder TP ranks
evidence_from_issue: encoder->decoder PP gradients summed instead of averaged when ETP < DTP
evidence_from_fix: _handle_tensor_list reduced via torch.stack(...).sum(dim=0); the fix is mean(dim=0): summing scaled the encoder gradient by the TP-fanout factor

relation_statement: Each step's observed gradient norm must be incorporated exactly once into the grad-norm EMA update (the EMA must not be updated from itself) whenever adaptive clipping is active.
observable_signal: grad_norm_exp_avg trajectory vs an EMA recomputed from the logged per-step grad norms; an EMA that never responds to grad-norm changes witnesses the self-referential update.
validity_precondition: Adaptive gradient clipping with grad_norm_exp_avg tracking enabled
evidence_from_issue: grad_norm_exp_avg EMA self-referential update — adaptive clipping broken
evidence_from_fix: (no root_cause text provided; inferred from title: EMA updated from its own previous value instead of the new grad-norm observation)

relation_statement: The logged auxiliary (MTP) loss must accumulate contributions from every iteration within the logging window rather than keeping only the last iteration's value.
observable_signal: logged MTP loss vs recomputed average of per-iteration losses over the log_interval window
validity_precondition: Multi-Token Prediction enabled with log_interval > 1
evidence_from_issue: MTP per-layer loss overwritten instead of accumulated when log_interval > 1
evidence_from_fix: save_loss_to_tracker assigned total_loss_dict[name] = loss regardless of whether the key existed; only the most recent iteration's MTP loss survived instead of the average over log_interval steps

relation_statement: Each epoch must consume every training example exactly once (the dataset start offset must reset to 0 at each epoch boundary) in multi-epoch training.
observable_signal: Per-epoch consumed-sample count vs dataset length, or dataset.start_index at epoch start (must be 0); skipping the first N instances of the new epoch witnesses the violation.
validity_precondition: max_epochs > 1 and an epoch boundary reached during training
evidence_from_issue: Multi-epoch training does not reset dataset.start_index, so the next epoch resumes from the previous epoch's offset
evidence_from_fix: on epoch rollover Trainer reset epoch counters and reshuffled but never reset dataset.start_index; the IterableDataset skipped the first global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch instances, silently dropping them

relation_statement: Cached rotary sin/cos tensors must be cast to match the query/key compute dtype before use under mixed-precision training.
observable_signal: Dtype of pos_sin/pos_cos at the point of application vs q/k dtype (fp32 cache meeting bf16/fp16 activations witnesses the mismatch).
validity_precondition: Mixed-precision (bf16/fp16) training with rotary position embeddings using a cached sin/cos table
evidence_from_issue: RoPE sin/cos missing type_as — dtype mismatch in mixed precision
evidence_from_fix: pos_sin/pos_cos cached in float32, not cast to match q_ dtype (bf16/fp16)
